title: Broccoli and Bacon Slaw
subtitle: Raw broccoli slaw with crispy bacon, sunflower seeds and a sweet-sharp dressing
excerpt: Finely shredded raw broccoli with crispy bacon lardons, red onion and sunflower seeds, dressed in a honey mustard mayo. Raw broccoli holds its texture for days and stays crunchier than cabbage.
sourceNotes: Broccoli slaw became popular in American home cooking in the 1990s as an alternative to traditional coleslaw. The use of raw broccoli rather than cabbage was particularly common in the southern United States, where the combination with bacon and a sweet dressing was well established. The dish came to British cookbooks through American food writing and became a regular feature of salad bar menus in the 2000s.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Add the bacon fresh before serving if making ahead.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the slaw base up to a day ahead; cook and add the bacon close to serving.

content.text: Broccoli slaw is the slaw that keeps its texture longest. Raw broccoli is denser than cabbage and does not release water in the same way; a broccoli slaw made a day ahead will still be pleasingly crunchy, where a cabbage coleslaw would have gone soft. The key is to shred the broccoli finely enough: the florets and stems grated or very finely chopped rather than broken into chunks.

items.prepNote: heads, about 600 g, florets and peeled stalk finely shredded

content.text: Cook {{lardons}} of lardons in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Leave to cool.

Stir together {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise, {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, {{wholegrain-mustard}} of wholegrain mustard, {{honey}} of honey, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Combine the shredded broccoli and red onion in a large bowl. Pour the dressing over and toss until coated. Leave for 15 minutes. Add the crispy bacon and {{sunflower-seeds}} of toasted sunflower seeds and toss again. Serve.

items.symptom: Broccoli is too tough to eat
items.fix: Shred the florets and peeled stalk very finely, either with a grater, food processor or sharp knife. Rough chunks are too hard to chew raw.

items.cause: Broccoli does not release much water so the dressing stays concentrated.
items.fix: Add a teaspoon of cider vinegar to loosen. The broccoli will not thin it for you the way cabbage does.

content.text: Broccoli slaw came to British cooking from America, where the raw broccoli and bacon combination is a potluck and buffet staple. It holds its texture better than cabbage slaw when made ahead. The bacon and sunflower seeds give it enough flavour to sit alongside plainly cooked meat or fish.
